rv.q: We hang on the narrator’s every word while fearing the bolts of darkness ricocheting through him.
Christopher Fitzgerald finds dark comedy, regret, and unexpected tenderness in Conor McPherson’s ‘The Good Thief.’
Fitzgerald doesn’t try to win you over—he just does.
So, it’s a pleasure to have the opportunity of seeing him showcased in such a challenging solo role, seeing him meeting the challenge so comfortably, so assuredly, so effortlessly, so winningly.
I'd say Fitzgerald's work here is more diligent than inspired, but even a diligent Christopher Fitzgerald is worth watching.
His performance is not to be missed.
The Good Thief is never less than riveting.

Fitzgerald's nonchalant delivery belies truly heinous acts... His performance explodes when he is pressured, trapped like an animal, yet becomes comforting and understanding when he assumes responsibility for others.
The result is a compelling reminder that sometimes all great theater needs is a good story and someone who knows how to tell it.
A story built to have audiences on edge here lacks tension.
It's a relatively slight play – say, compared to McPherson's 'The Weir' – but 'The Good Thief' is still good stuff.

cn.t: Critics largely praise Christopher Fitzgerald's magnetic solo performance in McPherson's early monologue, though some find the play itself slight. Direction and storytelling earn consistent applause.
